result.rule: When the description joins two activities with 'and' (for example, one party performs both actions for the same case) and gives no stated order between them, so both must be completed before the flow continues: Model the two activities as parallel branches: place a parallel gateway split before them and a parallel gateway join after them, so the next step starts only when both branches have completed. Do not model them as a sequence with an arbitrary order, and do not model them as alternatives.

When the description states one step that can be carried out in one of several named ways, joined by 'or' within the same clause, and the step is followed by a later step that depends on which way was chosen: Model each named way of carrying out the step as its own task. Place an exclusive gateway split before these tasks, with a labeled outgoing flow to each task. Join the alternative tasks with an exclusive gateway merge before the next step. Do not collapse the alternatives into one generic task, and do not keep only one of the named alternatives.

When the description names two or more alternative ways of signalling or performing the same need, where each alternative is a distinct action by a different actor or mechanism, and the alternatives must converge before the next step: Model each alternative as its own activity of the appropriate type on a separate outgoing branch of one exclusive gateway, then rejoin those branches with an exclusive merge before the next decision or step. Do not drop an alternative, and do not connect the gateway directly to the following step when an alternative is described as an action.

When the description states an action performed on a participant, and a later clause makes the next route depend on a choice that the same or another participant makes in response to that action: Model the stated action as its own task, placed in the order the description gives. Then model the dependent choice as an exclusive gateway after that task, with labeled branches for each stated alternative. Do not let the gateway replace the action, and do not omit the task because the branch conditions already refer to it. If the description states a further action for each alternative, give each branch its own task.

result.rule: Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
